doc.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022

chapter: Blood, Sweat & Tears and Horace Silver
title: Horace Silver's influence on Brecker as a bandleader
summary: Brecker leads like Silver, forming set lists and reining in long solos.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: What about you? Did you become, when you became a leader of a small group did you find yourself in that situation where you felt that’s not really what’s needed here?

Yeah. Yeah. I maybe wasn’t as hands-on as was Horace but I would — guys would get the idea not to play — so I’d say that, you know “Let’s do this tune, let’s do it short, we’ll stick it in here, we’ll stick it in there.” And I was pretty good at forming set lists. And Horace, I have to say, was really a big influence on when I started leading bands, probably a bigger influence than just about anybody else, just to rein in certain things so that tunes didn’t go on too long. I remember there was a jam session, Bennie was playing and Horace was sitting next to me and he whispered in my ear, “See Bennie’s tenor solo is getting long and he’s starting to repeat himself.” I’ve never forgot that too, so that still sticks with me.
